@graph.name: Japanese Shredded Cabbage Salad
@graph.description: The side that comes with almost anything fried in Japan — finely shredded raw cabbage, piled high next to tonkatsu or korokke. Cut it one way for soft, fluffy shreds; the other way for crisp and crunchy.

itemListElement.text: Cut a head of cabbage in half through the core, if you haven't. Cut out the core from ½ head green cabbage with a V-shaped cut. Tuck your thumb into this notch to hold the cabbage securely as you slice.

itemListElement.text: For Soft, Fluffy Shreds: Over a salad spinner, run a cabbage slicer across the veins (fibers) on the cut face of the cabbage half, shaving in long, even strokes.

itemListElement.text: Once the cabbage piece becomes too small to hold safely, switch to a knife and finely shred the rest.If using a knife from the start: Roll up the cabbage leaves tightly and slice them into fine shreds.

itemListElement.text: Rinse the shredded cabbage under running water. For Soft, Fluffy Shreds: Skip the soak and proceed directly to draining.For Crisp, Crunchy Shreds: Soak in ice water for 2–3 minutes first. Drain the cabbage thoroughly in a salad spinner, then fluff the shreds with your fingers to separate them. Toss in 1 Japanese or Persian cucumber (julienned), if using.Nami's Tip: Don't soak the cabbage for more than a few minutes, or it will lose its nutrients and flavor.

itemListElement.text: Mound the cabbage on a plate next to fried dishes like Korokke or Tonkatsu, and drizzle with Japanese Sesame Dressing, Wafu Dressing, or your favorite Japanese salad dressing right before serving.Nami's Tip: Dress the salad at the table, not in the kitchen. Cabbage begins to release water within 10 minutes of being dressed.

itemListElement.text: Line a container with a damp, tightly wrung-out paper towel, add the cabbage, and cover with a second damp towel before sealing. Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.

itemListElement.text: Press the shreds flat in a freezer-safe bag and lay it on a metal tray in the freezer. Store for up to 1 month. Thawed cabbage turns soft rather than crisp, so add it straight from the freezer to cooked dishes like stir-fries and soups.Nami's Tip: Metal pulls heat out faster, helping the cabbage freeze quickly and form smaller ice crystals. While the shreds will still soften when thawed, quick-freezing helps them hold their texture better.

@graph.name: Why does the direction I cut cabbage change its texture?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabbage leaves have a fiber running the length of each leaf. Cutting across them shortens the fibers for a soft, fluffy shred. Cutting along them keeps the fibers intact for a firmer, crunchier one, since nothing has been cut short.

@graph.name: Can I make Japanese Shredded Cabbage Salad ahead of time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Store shredded cabbage undressed in the fridge, or freeze it raw for up to a month. Dress it right before serving so the shreds stay crisp instead of turning watery.

@graph.name: Why soak the cabbage in ice water?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shredding drives moisture out of the cut surfaces, and soaking puts it back and cold water firms it further. That's what makes the pile crisp. 2–3 minutes is enough. Cabbage's vitamin C and potassium dissolve in water, so avoid long soaking.

@graph.name: What are other ways to garnish this salad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Build out the shredded cabbage salad base by adding thinly sliced cucumber and carrot, then top with chopped green onion and sesame seeds for color, crunch, and nutty flavor.
